chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
that he disliked wearing the burtala (a deep cape)

key_terms.الْبُرْطُلَةِ: A deep cape or outer garment, often made of wool or thick fabric, worn in the pre-modern era.
key_terms.كَرِهَ: He disliked (indicating a non-forbidden but discouraged status in fiqh).
key_terms.لُبْسَ: Wearing (the act of putting on clothing).

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say about wearing the burtala?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) expressed dislike (karahat) for wearing the burtala, a distinctive deep cape or outer garment popular in the Abbasid era. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing Muslim identity from prevailing cultural norms and avoiding excessive imitation of non-Muslim elites, a theme of modesty and distinctiveness often discussed in fiqh al-muta'allaqat.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having dislike wearing Al-Burtala (a deep cape)’.
